findings.title: Rapid date picks: an older, slower response can overwrite the newer pick
findings.where: Header date picker (app.ts pickDate), any tab
findings.steps: On the Breadth tab pick 30 Oct, then at once 12 Nov (script: both clicks in one tick; the 30 Oct day file delayed by 2.5 s with a route handler to model a slow network).
findings.expected: The page ends on 12 Nov (the last choice)
findings.actual: After both loads the page shows 30 Oct: date button 'Fri 30 Oct · Close', pill 'Prices to Fri 30 Oct', headline 'above EMA50 on 30 Oct'. pickDate has no sequence guard (day = await get(...) then assigns), so the last response to arrive wins, not the last click.
findings.evidence: probe t21 output ['Fri 30 Oct · Close', 'Prices to Fri 30 Oct', 'above EMA50 on 30 Oct ...']; apps/edge-bff/sector/src/app.ts:152-157
